methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops offered by a Norfolk native directly target skill distribution outside traditional tech hubs, suggesting grassroots capability-building that could counter concentration dynamics if sustained at scale.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents institutional investment in deep AI literacy outside NoVA/Richmond metros, potentially seeding distributed expertise networks in smaller markets if it extends beyond campus boundaries.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: The VCU-AI Ready RVA partnership explicitly targets community-wide AI education and innovation, signaling intentional efforts to broaden both depth and distribution within Richmond's ecosystem rather than concentrating capability in elite institutions.

signals.title: NoVa lawmakers take AI cash while residents resist data centers - opensecrets.org
signals.signal_reading: Resident resistance to data centers despite lawmaker support reveals a disconnect between infrastructure concentration and local capability development—NoVA gains physical AI infrastructure while communities may not gain proportional skills or economic benefits.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI pressure on Richmond's young workforce indicates concentrated demand for advanced skills in metro areas, likely accelerating talent stratification between workers who can upskill rapidly and those who cannot access training pathways.
